Sorry, you sound like you know hosting, but you’ve clearly never used Glacier yourself.

Downloading an archive from Amazon Glacier

Downloading an archive is an asynchronous operation. You must first initiate a retrieval job of a specific archive. After receiving the job request, Amazon Glacier prepares your archive for download which typically takes between 3-5 hours.

Glacier is for putting things away when you’re sure they do not need to be retrieved on-the-fly.

It’s great for long-term archival, on the order of months or years. It’s not so great for daily or even weekly backups if you might need to access them in a hurry; you’re better off keeping those on-site or on a more accessible service like S3, and only pushing them to Glacier after every month.

And it’s — to borrow a phrase — fucking literally retarded to use Glacier for a publicly-accessible site where you can’t predict when any one file may be requested regardless of age. An image host with a 3-5 hour wait to view older images would not do very well, I think. And not just the time, but the cost of retrieval on Glacier is much higher than the cost of storage, and higher than regular bandwidth costs.
